disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's detached per-workflow daemon — spawned by daemon-registry, owning its own HTTP control surface, lockfile, session and claim loop — is replaced by a FOREGROUND `cli worker <workflow-id> --pool-index <positive-int> [--drain]` process. Control moves off HTTP onto the one idempotent actor-stamped command family plus the authority's own claim leases. Each worker start owns a durable process record under .tracker/locks/workers; D181 strictly aggregates those records into one restore-safety observation while identity collision remains the authority lease's job. There is no per-daemon stdout log file: a worker's events reach the operator only through the ONE projection.

Legacy's per-workflow subcommands and system probes close one at a time as each workflow migrates, and ref workflow-model §1.6.3 requires behavioural CLI fixtures plus help output for the whole family before cutover.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Legacy's dedicated POST /api/daemon/stop is replaced by the ONE idempotent actor-stamped command endpoint (POST /api/v1/commands) carrying the `worker-browser` family's stop-worker type, so every product mutation is validated by the same authority-transactional kernel instead of by a per-action route with its own ad-hoc checks.

disposition.reason: There is no per-INSTANCE stop. The command union's stop-worker addresses a worker by workflow scope, not by a spawned daemon instance id, because a rebuild worker is a foreground process holding a durable claim lease and a per-start process record aggregated by D181 rather than a supervised detached daemon. Naming an instance would need a supervisor the rebuild does not have, and whether one is wanted is decided by how multi-worker operation actually behaves once real workflows run — so it closes with them, not ahead of them.

disposition.differencesAccepted: Enqueue is TWO steps, not one: POST /api/v1/start-plans mints a confirmable plan that retains the exact raw JSON ingress beside the schema-bound canonical snapshot and binds both schema hashes plus the canonical digest (D109), and POST /api/v1/commands then consumes that plan under the `start` family inside its own authority transaction (D113). A single fire-and-forget enqueue cannot bind the confirmation revision the terminal authority later requires.

This legacy module registers no route: it assembles the dashboard row payload for the entries SSE topic inside the route layer, and caches cross-workflow counts beside it. The rebuild builds every row and every total INSIDE the one projection (D81, and D180 for the range aggregates), so there is no second assembly path and no separate count cache that could disagree with the day it summarises.

disposition.reason: The rebuild has no general artifact-bytes endpoint for newly produced workflow files. Every remaining consumer — downloaded CRM/SharePoint documents, OnBase uploads, OCR page images — arrives with a phase-3 workflow, so this closes there rather than in 2i.

POST /api/v1/commands covers plan/spawn/stop/pause/resume-worker, refresh/reopen-browser and the run family (retry, cancel, bump, hide), and queue depth is `statusCounts` on GET /api/v1/dashboard. NOT built: browser kill/focus/check/screenshot/auto-recovery, worker drain over the wire (it exists only as the CLI's --drain flag), and every bulk cancel/retry/delete. Every one of those is a fact about operating MANY runs at once, and the rebuild has two workflows and no run corpus, so their consumer arrives with the migrations — which is also where a bulk affordance can be proved against real volume rather than a fixture.

The cross-run search over runs, entries and failure fingerprints is NOT built: its consumer is a corpus of runs, and the rebuild has produced two, so shaping a search surface now would fix its ranking and its facets against nothing. It closes as the migrations produce the corpus.
